newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE ready to probe 4,700-4,710 area.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE ready to probe 4,700-4,710 area.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will probe the 4,700 level on Wednesday and may try to feels its way up to around 4,710, technical analysts said.
From its slovenly manner on Tuesday when it see-sawed within a 16 point range, there remains a lack of purpose in the market, they added.

And although last night's bounce on Wall Street will have UK stocks nudging higher at the start of trading, doubts may creep back into investors minds about allowing the market to roam too far above 4,700 without the assistance of the bonds market.
By 0728 GMT, the FTSE was indicated up 13.1 at 4,694.7.

"Unless bond yields improve later in the day, the FTSE may repeat its dithering action," said one analyst who noted that the UK's 10 year benchmark gilt yield was up 7.22 percent on Tuesday compared with 7.09 percent a week ago.
In New York on Tuesday, the 30 year long bond was up 7.022 percent compared with around 6.91 percent last week.

A daily bar chart of the FTSE over the past week shows the UK equity market tracing out an upwardly sloping channel -- which is about 55 points wide and constructed from trendlines which join the market's intra-day highs and lows since May 20.

For the past few days the FTSE has appeared reluctant to leave the vicinity of of its 10-day moving average, and with mediocre breadth readings for the FTSE as well as short-term oscillators hovering around neutral, it will be difficult for the FTSE to make rapid upward progress, analysts said.

Despite this, investor sentiment has not turned decisively negative so that for the short-term at least, the FTSE will continue to follow the shallow upward direction given by those trendlines which are currently guiding it higher, they added.
